name: usb-through-esd-swap
prompt: I have a USB 2.0 host pair going to a USB connector through a 4-channel flow-through ESD part. The part is fictional for this exercise: each channel is an in pin and an out pin on opposite sides, the four channels are identical, and each channel has 3 ps delay and 0.05 dB loss in to out. For routing I want freedom to put D+ and D- on either channel pair (1,2) or (3,4), with either channel of the pair on D+. Wire it up with pin assignment, constrain the pair's intra-pair skew and total delay from host to connector, and prove the constraint actually applies, including what happens when the routing does not match an allowed mapping.

inputs.environment: Commands run from the repository root with python3 resolving to the interpreter of a venv that has jitx installed and its jitx entry point beside it; the check stages its own project under the system temp directory and starts and stops that project's runtime.

expected_output: A provider circuit around the ESD part offers one bundle covering both sides of a channel pair through provide.one_of, with four mappings: channels (1,2) and (3,4), each either way round, host side and connector side moving together, and no end-to-end D+/D- crossing. The consumer keeps the required bundle local, nets it to host and connector with +, puts a BridgingPinModel on each ESD channel, and applies ConstrainDiffPair(Topology(host.usb, conn.usb)) with a sourced skew limit and a labelled delay budget. Code routes on the ESD part's physical pins resolve the assignment. jitx design issues --satisfied shows Time and Skew lines for the straight and swapped-inverted routings, Code route dropped and No path for signal constraint for a routing that splits the pairs or whose two sides disagree, and No path with no measurement when unrouted.

assertions.text: the reference module and its check type-check against the installed jitx package
Straight: D+ on channel 1, D- on channel 2 resolves and measures time and skew end to end
SwappedInverted: D+ on channel 4, D- on channel 3 resolves to the inverted mapping and measures
Illegal: D+ and D- on different channel pairs drops a route, leaves a leg with no path, and measures no skew
SidesDisagree: host side on (1,2) and connector side on (3,4) drops routes and measures nothing
Unrouted: with no routes the assignment does not resolve and nothing measures

the answer routes the ESD part's physical pins rather than the required port, keeps the required port local (never on self), uses no >>, puts a BridgingPinModel on each ESD channel, offers no end-to-end D+/D- inversion, labels the part fictional and its values illustrative (or as given), and proves the constraint with jitx design issues --satisfied measured lines rather than a clean build
